accent.title: Accent colour
accent.help: The colour that marks what is selected or under way: the outline of the active panel, the timeline playhead, the frame around a selection. It changes nothing about what you make, only how the application shows you where you are. Leave it be to keep the theme’s own.

settings.accountDescription: One key per service, encrypted by the keychain.
settings.advancedDescription: What is only needed to understand a problem, or to start over.
settings.aiDescription: Which AI serves each operation. The studio here, Ollama here, or an online service you have a key for.
settings.applyHint: Writes the changes now, and leaves the window open

assistantSteps.title: Assistant chaining steps
assistantSteps.help: How many actions the assistant may chain for one request, when each depends on what the one before answered — find a file, open it, then place it in a scene. Every step is a billed round trip, so this number is the only thing keeping a misread request from running without end. Twelve covers most chains.

autosave.title: Save automatically
autosave.help: Writes open documents every thirty seconds, without waiting for your ⌘S. Whatever you have done since the last save then survives a power cut or a crash. Image documents are left out of it whatever this says: their layers are read back off the graphics card, and writing every thirty seconds would make drawing stutter.

boostFactor.title: Boost
boostFactor.help: What the speed is multiplied by while you hold the boost key. At 3 you go three times faster — enough to cross a large scene without changing the setting above.

settings.browseHint: Pick the folder in a system window
settings.cancelHint: Drops the pending changes, without closing the window

captionArrivals.title: Name fetched assets
captionArrivals.help: Automatically name an image that arrives without a useful name. Spends creative units.

settings.captureHint: Click, then press the chord to assign
settings.chordFree: No action uses this key: it is free.

concurrentJobs.title: Concurrent generations
concurrentJobs.help: How many creations work at the same time. The higher it is, the more you can start at once — but each may take longer to come back, and the service can turn away the ones beyond its limit. Three is a good balance.

settings.confirmHint: Writes the changes, then closes the window

copyMcpCommand.title: Connection command
copyMcpCommand.help: Copies the line to paste in a terminal to connect a client. It holds no port and no token, so it stays true for every launch to come.

copyMcpConfig.title: Configuration block
copyMcpConfig.help: Copies the same connection as JSON, for a client configured by a file rather than by a command. Like the command, it stays true for every launch.

density.title: Density
density.help: Sets how big the buttons are and how tall the rows sit. “Compact” fits more on screen; “Comfortable” leaves more air between things, which makes them easier to aim at with a mouse.

settings.dictationDescription: Speaking a text instead of typing it. Everything happens on this computer: nothing you say is sent anywhere.

dictationEnabled.title: Enable dictation
dictationEnabled.help: Offers a microphone button beside text fields, and puts the listening shortcut into service. Switched off, dictation loads nothing and never asks for microphone access.

dictationIdleUnload.title: Free the memory after
dictationIdleUnload.help: Minutes without dictating before the model is unloaded, returning around 700 MB of memory. It loads itself again on the next dictation, which takes a few seconds. Set it to 0 to keep it resident.

dictationMode.title: How it is triggered
dictationMode.help: “Hold” listens for as long as you keep the shortcut pressed and stops the moment you let go: it is the safest, since the microphone is never left open by mistake. “Toggle” starts on the first press and stops on the next, which rests the hand over a long dictation.

dictationModelFolder.title: Model folder
dictationModelFolder.help: Where to find a recognition model already on this disk, to use instead of the one the application downloads. Leave empty in the normal case.

dictationPreview.title: Preview while you speak
dictationPreview.help: How long, in milliseconds, between two previews of the text being spoken. The model does not write as the words come: every preview reads back everything said since the sentence began, and so costs computation. Set it to 0 to show only the settled text of each sentence.

dictationSilence.title: Silence that ends a sentence
dictationSilence.help: How much quiet, in milliseconds, before what you have just said counts as finished and gets transcribed. Raise it if your sentences are cut in half because you pause to think.

dictationThreads.title: Compute threads
dictationThreads.help: How many cores recognition may occupy. Higher is faster up to a point, but every thread is a core taken away from the rest of the application.

settings.discardBody: You changed settings without applying them. What would you like to do?
settings.discardTitle: Some settings have not been applied
settings.ffmpegFound: ffmpeg is available: proxies and waveforms will be prepared.
settings.ffmpegMissing: ffmpeg is still not found. Importing works, without proxy or waveform.

ffmpegPath.title: Path to ffmpeg
ffmpegPath.help: Where to find an ffmpeg to use instead of the one shipped with the application. Leave empty unless you insist on your own.

fieldOfView.title: Field of view
fieldOfView.help: How much the camera takes in, in degrees. A narrow angle pulls close and flattens, like a telephoto lens; a wide one shows far more but bends the edges. 60 is close to what an eye sees.

settings.findByChordHint: Click, then press a chord: the list keeps only what uses it

flySpeed.title: Fly speed
flySpeed.help: How fast the camera moves when you fly through the 3D view, in metres per second. Too slow and crossing the scene takes ten seconds; too fast and you shoot past it without seeing it.

fontScale.title: Text size
fontScale.help: Makes every text in the application bigger or smaller at once. 1 is the size it was drawn at; above that words get larger and less fits on screen; below, the opposite. Buttons keep their size: density is what handles those.

settings.generalDescription: The application’s language, and what it does when it opens.
settings.generationDescription: Generation queue and default models, per family.

gitBinary.title: Path to git
gitBinary.help: Where to find a git to use instead of the system one. Leave empty in nearly every case. A path holding a space is refused, and the application then behaves as it does when git is missing altogether.

settings.gitDescription: Version tracking of the project folder, by git. Your files only.

gitUserEmail.title: Author address
gitUserEmail.help: The address written beside the name in every recorded version. Leave empty to take the one git already knows.

gitUserName.title: Author name
gitUserName.help: The name written into every recorded version. Leave empty to take the one git already knows on this computer.

gizmoSize.title: Handle size
gizmoSize.help: The MOST room the transform handles take on screen. They never grow past the object they hold: on a small part they follow its size, and beyond that they keep to this share of the view rather than growing without end.

gridSize.title: Grid size
gridSize.help: How far the grid reaches, in metres, and therefore how many squares it has — a square is always one metre. Make it bigger for a wide scene, smaller for a little object sitting near the camera.

home.title: Show the home screen
home.help: The full-width screen the studio opens on: your projects, what you were working on, what is running, and what the models can do. Turn it off to go straight to the workspace you left. Which sections it shows, and in which order, is set on the home itself.

homeNews.title: Model news
homeNews.help: Reads the trending models and the articles published on Hugging Face, the host every weight of the catalogue already comes from. Unticked, the studio contacts nobody for this band.

installResolveBridge.title: DaVinci Resolve bridge
installResolveBridge.help: Drops a script into the folder Resolve reads, to import an edit written here from its own scripts menu. It appears without restarting Resolve. Removing it is done by hand, and Resolve only notices on its next start.
installResolveBridge.confirm: A script will be written into DaVinci Resolve’s folder, on this machine. Nothing else is touched.
installResolveBridge.missing: DaVinci Resolve was not found on this machine
installResolveBridge.missingDetail: Its folder does not exist, so nothing was written. Install Resolve, run it once, then come back here.

landing.title: Where a generation lands
landing.help: When a document of the same kind is already open. With nothing open, the result opens.
landing.newTab: In a tab of its own

language.title: Language
language.help: The language of every text in the application: menus, buttons, messages. “System” follows your computer’s own language. The change takes effect as soon as you click Apply or OK, with nothing to relaunch. It leaves your projects, and anything you write in them, alone.

logLevel.title: Log detail
logLevel.help: How much the application says about what it is doing, in the console. “Nothing” says nothing at all; “Errors” reports only what failed; “Everything” narrates each step, which helps to understand a problem and is chatty the rest of the time.

maxRetries.title: Max retries
maxRetries.help: When a generation fails because the network dropped or a server was busy, the application tries again on its own. This number says how many times before giving up. At 0 it never tries twice. An invalid API key is never retried: trying again would not fix it.

settings.mcpClosed: Shut: nothing is listening. Tick the setting above to open the door.

mcpDelegateAsset.title: Let it upload without asking
mcpDelegateAsset.help: Sending an image to your library, where it stays. It costs no creative units. Without this, every upload is asked about.

mcpDelegateBudget.title: Creative units spendable without asking
mcpDelegateBudget.help: What a client may spend in this window before the studio starts asking again. At zero, every spend is asked about. A generation the API declines to price is never started without you, whatever this holds.

mcpDelegateFiles.title: Let it touch files without asking
mcpDelegateFiles.help: Moving, renaming, binning, putting a git-tracked file back. The Explorer takes some of those back, never all. Without this, each one is asked about.

mcpDelegateRemote.title: Let it publish to a server without asking
mcpDelegateRemote.help: Sending a branch to a remote git repository. It is the only gesture that leaves this machine, and nothing here takes it back. Arm it knowingly.

settings.mcpDescription: The studio’s second door: another program on this machine — Claude Code, Cursor, any client speaking the MCP protocol — runs the same actions the assistant runs, from its own project. Shut to start with.

mcpEnabled.title: Drive the studio from outside
mcpEnabled.help: Opens a way in on this machine alone, through which a client such as Claude Code can run the same actions the assistant runs. Anything that spends or uploads asks for a yes on screen, exactly as it does here. Switched off, nothing is listening.

settings.mcpExampleGenerate: “Find a night skybox model, prepare the generation, but do not send it.”
settings.mcpExampleScene: “Put a sphere two metres to the right of the cube and light it warm.”
settings.mcpExampleTidy: “Sort this week’s rushes into one folder per day.”
settings.mcpGuardConsent: Anything that spends or uploads shows on screen and waits for your yes — except what you delegated above.
settings.mcpGuardLocal: The way in listens on this machine only: nothing from the network reaches it.
settings.mcpGuardOrigin: A request from a web page open in your browser is refused on that ground alone.
settings.mcpGuardToken: A new token every launch; a request without it is refused.
settings.mcpListening: Open: the studio is listening on 127.0.0.1:{{port}}, on this machine alone.
settings.mcpNothingToRedo: Only needs doing once. What you paste names the studio as a program to start, never an address to reach, so it keeps working across every launch — including the ones where the port and the token are new, which is all of them. A client already registered under the same name is replaced; there is nothing to remove first.
settings.mcpStepCopy: Copy the connection command, for a client driven from a terminal — or the configuration block, for a client that reads a file. Neither holds a port or a token.
settings.mcpStepOpen: Tick “Drive the studio from outside”, whenever suits you. The way in starts at once, and a client already configured finds it.
settings.mcpStepPaste: Paste it into a terminal open in your project, or the block into your client’s configuration file.
settings.mediaDescription: Preparation of imported files: proxies and waveforms.
settings.memoryArchiveHint: Sets it aside without erasing it: still readable, no longer given.
settings.memoryCompactHelp: Rewrites the file with one line per standing memory. This is where what was forgotten finally leaves the disk.
settings.memoryDescription: What the assistant has learned about your projects. What it learned about a project lives in that project’s folder and travels with it; what it learned about how you work stays on this machine.
settings.memoryEmbedHelp: Lets the assistant find a memory without knowing its exact words. Needs an embedding model installed.
settings.memoryEmbedNoModel: No embedding model is chosen. The search runs on words alone.
settings.memoryEmpty: The assistant has learned nothing here yet.
settings.memoryForgetHint: The forgetting is written into the file: nothing is erased, the trace remains.
settings.memoryGlobalHint: What the assistant learned about how you work. It never leaves this machine.
settings.memoryMergeHelp: Keeps the most important of each group saying the same thing, links the others to it and archives them. Nothing is erased.
settings.memoryMergeNone: Nothing says the same thing twice.
settings.memoryNoProject: Open a project to see what the assistant learned about it.
settings.memoryPinHint: A pinned memory is always given to the assistant, whatever the question.
settings.memoryProjectHint: What the assistant learned about the open project. That file travels with the folder.
settings.memoryPromoteHint: Copies this memory into the machine’s own, so it serves in every project of yours. What the project learned stays there too.
settings.memoryPurgeConfirm: Erase everything the assistant learned about this project?
settings.memoryPurgeHelp: Erases this project’s memory file, and everything the assistant had learned from it.
settings.memoryReindexHelp: Reads the file back and rebuilds the search index. Nothing learned is lost.
settings.memoryRestoreHint: The assistant may draw on it again.
settings.memoryStaleHelp: Sets aside what nothing has drawn on for six months. Pinned memories are never touched.
settings.memoryStopEmbedHelp: What has already been computed is kept.
settings.memoryTooNew: This file was written by a newer studio. Nothing has been changed.
settings.memoryUnpinHint: The assistant will only receive it when it answers the question asked.
settings.memoryUnreadable: The memory file could not be read whole. What follows may be incomplete.

openDevtools.title: Developer tools
openDevtools.help: Opens the technical console of the embedded browser. It shows the log messages and the errors. For troubleshooting only: nothing in there is needed to use the software.

openLogFolder.title: Technical log
openLogFolder.help: Opens the file manager on the log the studio writes on every launch. This is the file you will be asked for when something fails without saying anything on screen.

openSettingsFile.title: Settings file
openSettingsFile.help: Opens the file manager where your settings are saved. Useful to copy them before moving to another machine, or to send them to someone helping you.

projectsFolder.title: Projects folder
projectsFolder.help: The folder the application offers when you create or open a project. It moves nothing: projects already created stay where they are. Leave it empty to start from wherever you last were.

reduceMotion.title: Limit animations
reduceMotion.help: Turns off the small movements of the interface: panels appear at once instead of sliding in. Useful if animation tires you or makes you queasy, and on a slower machine where it stutters.

settings.requires: Has no effect while “{{setting}}” is off.

resetAll.title: Reset everything
resetAll.help: Puts EVERY setting back to a fresh install: theme, language, shortcuts, all of it. Your projects, images and edits are untouched — only the settings are. There is no going back.
resetAll.confirm: Reset every setting? Your projects are untouched, but this cannot be undone.

settings.restoreDefaultHint: Puts back the original value, the one from before any change
settings.searchResultHint: Goes to the setting, in the section it belongs to
settings.searchSectionHint: Opens the whole section, rather than the one result
settings.sectionHint: Shows the settings of this section
settings.sectionStagedHint: This section has changes that were not applied

shadowMapSize.title: Shadow detail
shadowMapSize.help: The side, in pixels, of the shadow map each shadow-casting light computes. Doubling it costs four times the memory: 2048 is plenty for a scene of a few objects, 4096 earns its keep when one light covers a whole set.

shadowQuality.title: Shadow softness
shadowQuality.help: The grain of a shadow’s edge. Hard cuts cleanly and costs the least; Soft smooths the edge. What throws a shadow, on the other hand, is decided object by object in the inspector.

shadows.title: Cast shadows
shadows.help: Works out the shadows the lights throw. Every light that casts one costs an extra render pass per frame: turning this off is the most direct way to lighten a heavy scene.

settings.shortcutConflict: Two actions are fighting over this key: only one will answer.
settings.shortcutsDescription: The keys that trigger each action. Click a key to replace it.
settings.showAllHint: Clears the filter and shows every shortcut again

showGrid.title: Show the grid
showGrid.help: The squared floor of the 3D view. It is not part of what you are making: it is a landmark for where things are and how high. Hide it to judge an image with nothing around it.

snapRotate.title: Rotate step
snapRotate.help: The angle of one step of rotation while snapping is on, in degrees. Rotation steps on from wherever it started: 15° gives twenty-four steps per turn, 90° quarter turns.

snapScale.title: Scale step
snapScale.help: How much the scale moves in one step while snapping is on. What is reachable is the multiples of the step: 0.1 lands exactly on tenths and halves, 0.25 on quarters.

snapSurfaceAlign.title: Align to surface
snapSurfaceAlign.help: While the surface snap is on, what you lay down lies along the slope it meets. Unchecked, it keeps its own orientation and only drops.

snapSurfaceOffset.title: Surface offset
snapSurfaceOffset.help: How many metres what you lay down floats above the surface. Zero rests it on contact; a few centimetres keep two faces from fighting over the same plane on screen.

snapTranslate.title: Move step
snapTranslate.help: How far an object travels in one step while snapping is on, in metres. Snapping itself is switched on from the scene toolbar; this only says how fine it is.

settings.spacesDescription: What only makes sense inside one space: the 3D view, the edit, the image.

startup.title: On opening
startup.help: What the application does when you launch it. “Reopen the last project” puts you back where you left off. “Open nothing” starts on an empty window, which is quicker and calmer if you juggle a lot of projects.

settings.storageDescription: Where your projects are kept on disk.

theme.title: Theme
theme.help: Picks the colours of the whole application. The dark theme rests the eyes over a long session in a dimly lit room; the light one reads better in broad daylight. “System” follows your computer’s own setting and switches on its own, for instance when evening comes.

settings.title: Settings

units.title: Display unit
units.help: The unit lengths are written and read in. One scene unit stays one metre whatever this says: it changes what is shown, never what the document holds.

viewportQuality.title: Viewport quality
viewportQuality.help: How finely the same frame is drawn. Nothing about the models or the images changes — only the number of pixels worked out. Performance also caps how fine the shadows get.
